content_blocks.text: The old lighthouse stood as a sentinel on the edge of the cliff, its weathered walls whispering tales of the sea to anyone who dared to listen. As the fog rolled in, thick and heavy, it seemed to speak in low, mournful tones, as if it held secrets too deep to share. In the dim light, the keeper, an elderly man named Elias, moved through the darkened rooms, his lantern casting long shadows across the walls. He paused at the top of the stairs, looking out over the churning waters below. The wind howled like a lost soul, and he shivered, despite the warmth of his coat. 'Another night,' he muttered, 'another night to watch the waves.'
